title.narrative: Enhancing the Resilience of the State Demographic Register of Ukraine - Tallinn Mechanism

description.narrative:
TheTallinn Mechanism is a platform to strengthen Ukraine's cyber defense by making international assistance more effective and coordinated among partner countries. ITwas launched in 2023 as an international response to growing cyber threats and russia's ongoing aggression.
One of the constant targets of Russia’s war of aggression is Ukraine’s cyber capabilities, both in the military and civilian domains. It is therefore important to support Ukraine’s cyber defence, as well as its ability to restore and develop the relevant infrastructure. Civilian sector support is coordinated through the Tallinn Mechanism, which held its first meeting in Ukraine on 24 April. At this meeting, Estonia handed over the chairmanship to France and Sweden for the next six months.
The project aims to enhance the cybersecurity and operational resilience of Ukraine’s State Demographic Register and selected government institutions through targeted technical upgrades and institutional capacity building. Key activities include the modernization of IT infrastructure, implementation of advanced security solutions, and delivery of specialized training for staff and cybersecurity professionals. The intervention is co-created with Ukrainian beneficiaries to ensure alignment with national priorities and sustainability of outcomes. All procurement and implementation activities strictly adhere to relevant legislation and best practices, with robust risk management and transparency measures in place. The project is designed to enable long-term maintenance and local ownership, supporting Ukraine’s continued digital resilience beyond the project’s duration.
